timeline.event: Release 4.33.3 of the auth gateway starts rolling out to production.
Error rates on the auth gateway begin to climb.
The AuthGatewayLoginFailures alert fires and pages the on-call engineer.
Tomasz Okafor acknowledges the page and opens an incident channel.
The team decides to roll back release 4.33.3.
The rollback completes and error rates return to baseline.
Sofia Achterberg declares the incident resolved after monitoring stays clean.

root_cause: Release 4.33.3 rotated the token-signing key before the new key had reached every gateway node, so half the nodes rejected valid sessions.
contributing_factors: Key distribution and key activation were one step instead of two.
The health check tested only the gateway's own endpoint, not a real login.
went_well: The incident channel kept a clear written timeline.
Customer support had a holding statement out quickly.
went_badly: Nobody owned the shared config file that changed.
The status page was updated well after customers started reporting errors.

action_items.action: Add contract tests for header and config-only changes
Add a review rule for changes to the shared config file
Lower the alert threshold and add a second, symptom-based alert
